stages.evidence: 15 failed logins in the first minute from one source (10.20.4.15); no success yet - password guessing / spraying. First indicator of the incident.
stages.risk: Medium: no access gained yet, but it is the earliest and cheapest point to stop the attack.

stages.evidence: 21 more failures from the same source, 36 in total within 3 min; the dataset raises severity to High - the attack is persistent, not a typo.
stages.risk: High: failure count is rising 15 -> 21, so a success is likely next.

stages.evidence: A successful login from the same IP 10.20.4.15 right after 36 failures = valid credentials obtained (account takeover). All later events follow within 14 minutes.
stages.risk: Critical in my assessment (dataset: High): attacker is now authenticated; this is the point of no return.

stages.evidence: 320 files modified, source still 10.20.4.15, three minutes after the login - bulk write activity typical of ransomware staging/encryption start.
stages.risk: Critical: integrity of research data is being destroyed.

stages.evidence: CPU 95% on Research-Server-01 one minute after the file burst - encryption routine is running (cryptographic work is CPU-bound).
stages.risk: High: confirms the file activity is automated; resource exhaustion also degrades the service.

stages.evidence: 1,200 files encrypted: 3.75x the 320 files modified at 09:07, i.e. about 400 files/min over the 3 minutes since 09:07.
stages.risk: Critical: impact reached; data unavailable without a backup.

stages.evidence: Backup deletion attempt from the same host 2 min after encryption - the attacker removes the recovery path so that ransom is the only option.
stages.risk: Critical: if it succeeds, RPO and RTO targets become impossible.

stages.evidence: Outbound connection from the server to an unknown IP - possible command-and-control or data theft (double extortion).
stages.risk: High: a confidentiality breach may carry personal-data and research-IP obligations.

stages.evidence: Database access spike two minutes after the outbound connection - data collection/staging before upload.
stages.risk: High: mass reads of the research database; scope of theft unknown.

stages.evidence: Antivirus disabled (needs administrative rights) - defence evasion that keeps the foothold and blocks clean-up. Mapped to the nearest allowed stage.
stages.risk: Critical: attacker holds admin rights and detection is now blind on this host.

risks.justification: A deletion attempt at 09:12 proves intent (likelihood 4). Impact 5: it removes the only recovery path - without backups ransomware becomes unrecoverable.
Encryption of 1,200 files is already in the dataset; likelihood 4 (not 5) because recurrence depends on the controls added. Impact 5: research data and service unavailable.
Occurred: 36 failures then a success within 3 minutes; no MFA evidence in the dataset. Impact 4: full account takeover but initially limited to one user's rights.
Disabling antivirus needs admin rights, so escalation very likely already happened (4). Impact 4: attacker can switch off defences and reach other systems.
Outbound connection and DB spike are indicators, not proof of theft (likelihood 3). Impact 4: research IP and personal data, with regulatory and reputation cost.

alerts.message: 36 failed logins in 3 min - brute force
successful login after 36 failures from 10.20.4.15 - suspected account takeover
320 files modified in 1 min - ransomware behaviour
database request rate far above baseline - possible data collection
